primary_claim: Reasoning models (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, DeepSeek R1) only verbalize their use of a slipped problem-solving hint in their chain-of-thought a minority of the time (25% and 39% on average respectively), showing CoT is often unfaithful to the reasoning actually used.
stated_future_work: Find a way to make CoT more faithful
Gather evidence for higher faithfulness in more realistic scenarios
Develop other measures to rule out misbehavior when the CoT is unfaithful
limitations_stated: Monitoring CoTs is unlikely to reliably catch rare, catastrophic behaviors, at least in settings like ours where CoT reasoning is not necessary for the task
quote: We found Chains-of-Thought largely aren’t “faithful”: the rate of mentioning the hint (when they used it) was on average 25% for Claude 3.7 Sonnet and 39% for DeepSeek R1.
